title: CPython IDLE project series with permitted LLM support
summary: Junior and senior software-engineering students build, modify, and extend the CPython IDLE codebase before completing a team-designed feature. Instructors permit and demonstrate ChatGPT and Copilot; students submit code through pull requests plus process journals and design documents that expose how they navigated and changed the system.

sources.title: Working with Large Code Bases: A Cognitive Apprenticeship Approach to Teaching Software Engineering
sources.evidence_quote: For the first half of the term, the students worked on three individual projects ... In the second half, they proposed their own project in teams of three.

assessment.summary: Build CPython, modify an IDLE feature, add a code-outline feature, and implement and present a team-proposed IDLE feature.
student_actions: Build CPython and configure the development environment.
Modify IDLE's Go To Line behavior.
Add a Show Code Outline feature.
Propose, implement, test, review, and present a team feature.

student_role.description: Students may use ChatGPT and Copilot as just-in-time resources; process journals document the tools used.

grading.method: Staff review pull requests, requirements, design documents, process journals, team code reviews, presentation, and Q&A; students may address review feedback within three days.
grading.resubmission: Students can address TA code-review feedback within three days to recover points.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.
